VCLJ: Raag Tilang, in Ghar 3, the bani of Guru Nanak Dev ji.
G30W: Akal Purakh is One and is found by the grace of the Satguru.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but One God. By True Guru's grace is He obtained.
S8UM: Maia pahia = it has been given the mordant of Maya. Pahia = the mordant has been applied. Pah = the mordant. {Note: before a fast colour is put upon cloth, a mordant of salt, alum or soda is applied. Soda, salt or alum is boiled in water and the cloth is dipped into it; then the dye is boiled in water and that mordanted cloth is put into it}. Lab = with lab, with the relish of the tongue. Labu = the relish of the tongue. Rangae leetra = has had it dyed.
The soul-bride to whose body the mordant of (attachment to) Maya has been applied, and who has then had it dyed with the relish of the tongue,
This body fabric is conditioned by Maya, O beloved; this cloth is dyed in greed.
My beloved, this body cloth mercerized by worldly attachments is dyed in greed.
O my beloved husband! This (tan) subtle garment that is the mind has been mordanted with the mordant that is the deceit of Maya, and has been dyed with the dye that is (lab) greed.

R80H: Chola = the robe of the soul, the body. Cholra = an ugly robe. Merai kant = to my husband. Bhavai = is pleasing. Dhan = the woman, the soul-bride. Sejai = upon the bed (of the Lord), at the Lord's feet. Jae = may reach. ||1||
That soul-bride cannot reach the feet of her husband-Lord, because this robe (of the soul, this body, this life) is not pleasing to the husband-Lord. ||1||
My Husband Lord is not pleased by these clothes, O Beloved; how can the soul-bride go to His bed? ||1||
My beloved, such a cloak pleases not my Groom How can the bride go to His couch?

O my (kant) husband, supremely beloved Waheguru! Such a robe, dyed with greed, is not pleasing to you; then how shall this (dhan) faith that is the seeker come to be upon the bed and become one with you? The meaning being that this creature, seized by greed for material things, can never attain you. ||1||
JH35: Miharvana = O merciful Lord! Hanu = I.
O merciful Lord! I go as a sacrifice, I am devoted,
I am a sacrifice, O Dear Merciful Lord; I am a sacrifice to You.
I am a sacrifice, O Beneficent Lord, I am a sacrifice to You.
Therefore, O husband! I go as a sacrifice upon you with my mind; again, O merciful one! I go as a sacrifice with my body also.
TKBP: I go as a sacrifice to those who remember your Name.
I am a sacrifice to those who take to Your Name.
I am a sacrifice to those, who take Your name.
Again, I go as a sacrifice upon those holy servants who go on uttering your Name at all times.
XRXJ: Lain = they take. Sad = always. ||1|| Rahau ||
Those people who take your Name, I go as a sacrifice to them for ever. ||1|| Rahau ||
To those who take to Your Name, I am forever a sacrifice. ||1||Pause||
They, who utter Yours name, to them, I am ever a sacrifice. Pause.
And again, upon those who take your Name I go as a sacrifice a hundred times, or for ever. ||1|| Rahau ||
GCFS: Kaia = the body. Ranngan = the open vessel in which the dyer dyes cloth, the vat. Theeai = may become. Majeeth = {Note: people used to boil madder and dye cloth with it. This colour was fast}.
(But yes!) If this body were to become the (dyer's) vat, and, O friend! if into it were put the Lord's Name-dye, which is fast like madder,
If the body becomes the dyer's vat, O Beloved, and the Name is placed within it as the dye,
If the body becomes the dyer's vat, the name is put into it as madder,

O beloved! If this body were to become the vat — that is, if one were to become an aspirant furnished with the means — then let the dye of the madder that is the Name be put into this vat that is the body.
2EXM: and then if the master-Lord himself, becoming the dyer, were to give (the soul-bride's mind) the dip of that dye, then such a colour takes hold as was never seen before. ||2||
and if the Dyer who dyes this cloth is the Lord Master - O, such a color has never been seen before! ||2||
and the Lord, the Dyer, Himself dyes, then, such a colour would appear, as had never been seen O beloved.

The dyer, who is the Sahib the Satguru — if he were ever to dye the robe that is the inner self in the dye of that madder which is the Name, then such a colour would take as had never been seen; the meaning being that the bliss of the self would be attained. ||2||
0CA2: O beloved (friend!) Those soul-brides whose (body-)robes (whose lives) have been dyed (with the Name-dye), the husband-Lord (ever) dwells beside them.
Those whose shawls are so dyed, O Beloved, their Husband Lord is always with them.
They, whose cloaks are thus dyed, O Beloved, the spouse is ever near them.
In the manner said above, those great souls whose robes that are the inner self have been dyed — O my beloved husband! Beside those soul-brides who are the holy servants you ever make your dwelling.
BZGR: O friend! Make this supplication before them on Nanak's behalf, that somewhere Nanak might obtain the dust of their feet. ||3||
Bless me with the dust of those humble beings, O Dear Lord. Says Nanak, this is my prayer. ||3||
O Lord, somehow bless Nanak with the dust of those persons. O Sire Nanak makes this supplication.
Sri Guru ji says: O Akal Purakh ji! This alone is my one (ardas) supplication — that if the dust of the feet of those holy servants be obtained by me, then I shall be fulfilled. ||3||
3U7V: Saje = he adorns. Nadar = the glance of mercy. Karei = he does, he makes.
The soul-bride upon whom the Lord himself casts his glance of mercy, he himself adorns her and he himself puts the colour (of the Name) upon her.
He Himself creates, and He Himself imbues us. He Himself bestows His Glance of Grace.
The Lord Himself creates, Himself stains and Himself He caste the merciful glance.

The one on whom this sight of mine falls, so that I see you alone as the form of all — how it is that you yourself make one furnished with the means, you yourself bring one to the sight of knowledge of the dye in the madder that is the Name, or you yourself bring it forth, and you yourself dye one in the colour of the Name by your glance of grace.
DSNF: Kaman = the woman, the soul-bride. Ravei = he enjoys, he unites her with himself. ||4||1||3||
O Nanak! That soul-bride is dear to the husband-Lord; the Lord himself joins her to his own feet. ||4||1||3||
O Nanak, if the soul-bride becomes pleasing to her Husband Lord, He Himself enjoys her. ||4||1||3||
Nanak, if the bride becomes pleasing to her Bridegroom, He enjoys her of His own accord.

Sri Guru ji says: when this soul-bride who is the seeker, having this sight, becomes pleasing to you, O husband! then (ape hi ravei) you yourself enjoy her; the meaning being that you make her one with yourself.
PW99: Iani = an ignorant girl. Ianri = a very ignorant girl. Ianriae = O very ignorant soul! Manra = an ugly pride. Kae = why? Karehi = you do.
O very ignorant soul! Why do you take such ugly pride?
O foolish and ignorant soul-bride, why are you so proud?
O silly woman, why takest you pride?
O ignorant woman who is the soul! For what (kae) do you take (manra) pride?
R64F: Ghar = in the house, within the heart. Rango = rangu, bliss. Kee = why?
The Lord is within your own heart-home; why do you not enjoy the bliss (of union) with him?
Within the home of your own self, why do you not enjoy the Love of your Lord?
Why enjoyest you not the love of God, in Your own home?

Hari is within your own body; why do you not enjoy his (rangon) bliss? As the authority — ☬ "Why do you go searching in the forest? ☬ He who dwells in all and is ever detached is contained within you."
C57E: Dhan kammliae = O simple soul-bride! Bahar = the outer world {Note: the difference between 'bahar' and 'baharu' is worth keeping in mind}.
O simple soul-bride! The husband-Lord is dwelling near (you, within you); why do you go searching the outer world (the forests and the rest)?
Your Husband Lord is so very near, O foolish bride; why do you search for Him outside?
Your Bridegroom is quite near, O foolish bride, What for searchest you abroad?

The husband, who is Waheguru, is exceedingly near; indeed, he is your own very self. (Dhan) O simple woman who is the seeker! What are you searching for outside? As it is said — ☬ "That Lord is nearer than the near." ☬ If it be asked, how is the husband to be obtained? To that he says:
M3HQ: Bhav ka = of love. Salaee = the collyrium-rod with which collyrium is applied to the eyes.
(If you are to have the sight of him, then into your eyes of knowledge) put the rods of the collyrium of the fear and reverence (of the Lord), and make the adornment of the Lord's love.
Apply the Fear of God as the maascara to adorn your eyes, and make the Love of the Lord your ornament.
Put the slave needles of God's fear into yours eyes and make the decoration of the Lord's love.
This fear of Waheguru ji that is to be borne — apply the rods of collyrium into these eyes that are the intellect, that is, put them in, and take on the adornment of love.
1638: The soul-bride is known to be blessed with good fortune and joined to the Lord's feet only then, when the husband-Lord bears love for her. ||1||
Then, you shall be known as a devoted and committed soul-bride, when you enshrine love for your Husband Lord. ||1||
Then alone shall you be known as devoted wife, attached to your spouse, if you bearest Him love.

O blessed soul-bride who is the seeker! Then you will be known to be intent upon that Waheguru, when that (sahu) husband bears love for you. ||1|| ☬ Question: why does this woman who is the seeker not attain him by her own strength? To that he says:
0YJB: Kia kare = what can she do? Kant na bhavai = if she is not pleasing to the husband.
(But) what can even the ignorant soul-bride do, if that soul-bride is simply not pleasing to the husband-Lord?
What can the silly young bride do, if she is not pleasing to her Husband Lord?
What can the silly young bride do, if she pleases not her Groom?
She who is not pleasing to that husband — (iani bali) the ignorant woman who is the seeker, without fear and love, what can she do?
QE0G: Karan palah = {करूणाप्रलाप} entreaties, lamentations. Sadhan = the soul-bride.
However many entreaties such a soul-bride may go on making, she simply cannot find the palace-home of the husband-Lord.
She may plead and implore so many times, but still, such a bride shall not obtain the Mansion of the Lord's Presence.
Though she may make good many implorations, you, such a bride cannot obtain her spouse's mansion.
She makes many efforts, such as loud weeping, but without the mercy of Hari that woman can never attain the form.
K3RV: Karma = karam, grace. Dhavai = may run about.
(The truth of it is that) however much the soul-bride may run about, without the Lord's glance of mercy nothing at all is gained.
Without the karma of good deeds, nothing is obtained, although she may run around frantically.
Without good deeds, nothing can be obtained though she may run about a great deal.
Though she may run about ever so much, without desireless action not even (kichh) the least little is obtained.
S302: If the soul-bride remains engrossed only in the relish of the tongue, in greed and in pride (and the rest), and remains ever drowned in (attachment to) Maya,
She is intoxicated with greed, pride and egotism, and engrossed in Maya.
Inebriated with avarice, covetousness and pride, she is engrossed in worldliness.
(Lab) the greed for food, (lobh) the greed for hoarding, and the (mati) intoxication of the vices such as pride — absorbed within Maya, upon what is she intent?
122U: Ini bati = by these things. Kaman = the woman. ||2||
then by these things the husband-Lord is not found. That soul-bride has remained ignorant (who is engrossed in the vices and yet supposes that she can please the husband-Lord). ||2||
She cannot obtain her Husband Lord in these ways; the young bride is so foolish! ||2||
By these things the Groom is obtained not, Ignorant is the young bride.

By these things of the vices spoken of above the husband Waheguru is not obtained, and therefore the woman who is the seeker (bhaee) has remained ignorant. ||2|| ☬ Question: how is this ignorant woman to attain that husband?
W2GV: (Those to whom the husband-Lord has come — by all means) go and ask those blessed with good fortune by what things the husband-Lord is found,
Go and ask the happy, pure soul-brides, how did they obtain their Husband Lord?
Go and ask the chaste brides, by what actions is the Spouse obtained.
(Vahai) those blessed women who are the holy servants — go to them and ask, by which (bati) words is the husband obtained.
FUWD: Hikmat = cleverness. Hukam = force, high-handedness, compulsion.
(They give this very answer, that) give up cleverness and force; whatever the Lord does, accept it as good (bow your head to it),
Whatever the Lord does, accept that as good; do away with your own cleverness and self-will.
Whatever the Lord does, accept that as good and do away with your cleverness and will.

Then those blessed holy servants give this answer: whatever that husband Waheguru does, accept it as good alone; (hikmat) our cunning, and (hukam) the saying "O Parmesar! Why have you done thus, now do it so" — let us raise these from the mind; the meaning being that we should remain glad in the will of Waheguru.
64DS: Ja kai prem = through the love of him. Tau = his.
Join your mind to the feet of that Lord through whose love the commodity of the Name is obtained,
By His Love, true wealth is obtained; link your consciousness to His lotus feet.
Attach you your mind to His feet, by whose love the wealth of emancipation is attained.
That Satguru through love for whom (padarath) knowledge is attained — then let the mind be joined to his lotus feet.
0R7E: Mano = manu, the mind. Parmal = fragrance.
Do what the husband-Lord commands, hand over your body and mind to him — that is all! Use this fragrance (for the soul).
As your Husband Lord directs, so you must act; surrender your body and mind to Him, and apply this perfume to yourself.
Do you that, what is spouse bids you. Surrender your body and soul to Him and apply you such a perfume.
Whatever the master says, let us do it, let us surrender our body and mind to him alone; let us apply the sandal of such a resolve.
G09R: Ev = in this way. Kahah = they say. ||3||
Those blessed with good fortune say this very thing, that O sister! By these things alone is the husband-Lord found. ||3||
So speaks the happy soul-bride, O sister; in this way, the Husband Lord is obtained. ||3||
Thus says the true wife, O sister. By these means the Bridegroom is obtained.
In this way those blessed holy servants say: O sister who are the seeker! By these things that master is attained. ||3||
E5PW: Ap = the sense of self. Aur = any other effort. Kaisi chaturaee = a useless cleverness.
The husband-Lord is found only then, when the sense of self is removed. Apart from this, any other effort is a useless cleverness.
Give up your selfhood, and so obtain your Husband Lord; what other clever tricks are of any use?
Efface your ownself and then shall you obtain the Groom. What can other cleverness avail?
Again, (ap gavaeeai) if "I" and "mine" be removed from the heart, then that husband is attained; and what is any cleverness of any other kind — that is, it is of no use at all.
PBTN: Lekhai = in the reckoning, fruitful. Naunidh = the nine treasures.
Know that day (of life) to be fruitful when the husband-Lord looks with the glance of mercy; the soul-bride upon whom he casts (the glance of mercy) has, as it were, found the nine treasures.
When the Husband Lord looks upon the soul-bride with His Gracious Glance, that day is historic - the bride obtains the nine treasures.
The day when the Spouse looks with grace is of signal accounts, and the bride obtains nine treasures.

When that husband Waheguru looks with the glance of grace, that very day is entered in the reckoning — the meaning being that that very day becomes fruitful; and she upon whom he has shown mercy, that woman who is the seeker has obtained the love of the master who is the form of the nine treasures.
DGX9: Sabhraee = one who has brothers, one honoured in the whole family.
O Nanak! That soul-bride who is dear to her husband-Lord is blessed with good fortune; she obtains honour and regard in the (world-)family.
She who is loved by her Husband Lord, is the true soul-bride; O Nanak, she is the queen of all.
She, who is the beloved of her Bridegroom, is the happy wife, Nanak, she is the queen of all.

In this way, that woman who is the seeker and who has become dear to her master Waheguru — she alone is the blessed one. Sri Guru ji says: she alone has become the chief queen of the king among all creatures; or, she is one who has brothers — that is, she is furnished with the qualities of the divine wealth.
UA6X: Rang = in the colour. Rati = dyed, coloured. Ah = day. Nis = night. Bhae = in bhau, in love.
She who remains dyed in the Lord's colour of love, who remains engrossed in poise, who remains absorbed day and night in the Lord's love,
Thus she is imbued with His Love, intoxicated with delight; day and night, she is absorbed in His Love.
Like this she remains imbued with pleasure, intoxicated with glee and day and night absorbed in the Lord's love.
In this way she who is dyed in bliss and is (mati) intoxicated with the state of (sahaj) peace, remains absorbed in love day and night.
Q96J: Sundar = beautiful. Saee = that very woman. Saroop = one of lovely form. Bichkhan = one of understanding {विचक्षण = of keen intellect}. Sa = that woman ||4||2||4||
She alone is beautiful, she is of lovely form, she is of understanding and she is called wise. ||4||2||4||
She is beautiful, glorious and brilliant; she is known as truly wise. ||4||2||4||
She is spoken of as comely, beauteous and intelligent and she alone is wise.

That woman who is the seeker is (sundar) one of lovely form and (bichkhan) one who has, in particular, the eyes of knowledge and detachment; and she alone is called clever in every way. ||4||2||4|| ☬ At the time when Sri Guru Nanak Sahib ji went to Emnabad he halted outside the town itself. Bhai Mardana went into the town for food. The Pathans slighted him, and he came back again bringing Bhai Lalo ji with him. Then, seeing the slighting of his own servant, in wrath against the Pathans, and telling it to Lalo ji, he uttered a shabad foretelling what was to come: the full account has been given in Raag Asa, look it up there.

M695: Kaun = which? Taraji = the scales. Kavan = which? Tula = the weight. Saraf = the one who sets the value, the one who assays. Bulava = bulavan, may I call.
O Lord! There is no such scale and no such weight (as could take the measure of your qualities); there is no such assayer whom I might call (to take the measure of your qualities).
What scale, what weights, and what assayer shall I call for You, Lord?
What is the scale, and what are the weights? What assayer shall I call for You, O Lord?

O Bhagvan! (Kaun) which scales and which tula — the small beam is what they call it — or which weight might there be, and which assayer might I call to weigh you, who might weigh you or make the assay?
GS9G: Kai pah = from whom? Deekhia = instruction. Leva = may I take. Mul karava = may I have the value set. ||1||
I see no such master from whom I might have your value set, or from whom I might learn the art of setting a value. ||1||
From what guru should I receive instruction? By whom should I have Your value appraised? ||1||
Who is the Guru, from whom I should receive instruction and by whom should I have yours worth appraised?
From which Guru might I take instruction, from whom might I have your price set — the meaning being that you are beyond price. ||1||
